name: Sotalol
summary: A non-selective beta-blocker with added class III potassium channel blockade, useful for atrial and ventricular arrhythmias but carrying a dose-related torsades risk.
mechanism: Non-selective beta-1/beta-2 adrenergic blockade combined with IKr potassium channel blockade, prolonging atrial and ventricular refractoriness.
pharmacodynamics: Prolongs QT interval and action potential duration; slows heart rate and AV conduction.

dosing.adult: 80 mg twice daily initially, titrated (usual maintenance 120–160 mg twice daily for VT; up to 160 mg twice daily for AF)
dosing.renalAdjustment: Extend dosing interval in renal impairment (e.g., once daily if CrCl 40–60 mL/min); avoid if CrCl <40 mL/min

safety.pregnancy: Use only if clearly needed (crosses placenta; no adequate data)
contraindications: Sinus bradycardia or heart block without pacemaker
warnings: Torsades de pointes — dose-related, especially with hypokalemia/hypomagnesemia or rapid titration
monitoring: ECG with QTc before and after each dose increase
safety.overdose: Bradycardia and hypotension; supportive care, pacing for severe bradycardia

clinicalPearls: Combines class III antiarrhythmic and beta-blocker effects in one drug.
Renally cleared — QTc monitoring during titration is mandatory, especially in older patients.
good: Patients needing both rate control and rhythm control who can tolerate beta-blockade.
bad: Patients with asthma, renal impairment, long QT, or unstable heart failure.
